USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Stopping treatment safely

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 35-year-old patient has been taking gabapentin regularly as adjunctive seizure treatment. He wants to discontinue it because of daytime sleepiness but has not yet changed his dose. Which plan best reduces the risk associated with withdrawal?

  1. Stop every dose immediately without a plan
  2. Double the dose and then stop the next day
  3. Replace each dose with alcohol
  4. Take the entire weekly dose at once
  5. Arrange a clinician-guided gradual taper
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Arrange a clinician-guided gradual taper

Abrupt discontinuation can increase seizure frequency; the regimen should be tapered with appropriate clinical supervision.

Understanding the options

Arrange a clinician-guided gradual taper
Abrupt discontinuation can increase seizure frequency; the regimen should be tapered with appropriate clinical supervision.
Stop every dose immediately without a plan
Abrupt cessation can precipitate withdrawal and seizures.
Double the dose and then stop the next day
This increases exposure without providing a gradual taper.
Replace each dose with alcohol
Alcohol adds CNS depression and is not a withdrawal strategy.
Take the entire weekly dose at once
This risks toxicity and cannot maintain stable treatment.
